From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Package

**Process note:** I reviewed all 16 items, including those the Seller labels [STANDARD]. The "reviewer efficiency note" is the Seller's characterisation, not a record of agreement. Nothing in this package has been agreed. The disclosure is also stale: it speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026, so every open item needs a current status update. Figures below come from the Seller's disclosure and have not been verified.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap (open at 30%, about AUD 7.2m). Specific indemnities and fundamental and tax claims sit outside the cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30%. Accept 20% only if fundamental, tax and specific indemnities are carved out.
- **Reason:** The disclosed known items (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, Sandbar) already total about AUD 4.1m if pursued as warranty claims, roughly 86% of the proposed general cap, before the unquantified privacy matter and any Bluefen value loss.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** Claims must exceed AUD 25k, and only the excess above a AUD 250k deductible basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of about AUD 10k. A tipping basket of about 1% (AUD 240k), so that once exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar. Related claims aggregate as one claim. Thresholds do not apply to specific indemnities, fundamental or tax claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible. Counter with a tipping basket.
- **Reason:** A AUD 250k deductible means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of any warranty loss, and a AUD 25k de minimis excludes smaller claims entirely.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion, and that limitation applies to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties, so the window covers a full audit and year-end cycle. Tax claims run for the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, or 6 years. Fundamental claims run for 6 years. Notification should be followed by proceedings within a set period.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months for general warranties, with separate longer periods for other categories.
- **Reason:** Privacy, tax and Ironquay issues may not surface until after an 18-month window has closed.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares, no encumbrances) capped at the purchase price, with a 6-year limit and no basket or de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title is what the Buyer is paying for, and a AUD 4.8m cap with an 18-month limit would leave a later title defect largely unremedied.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply exclusive-remedy, limitation and non-reliance language to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that nothing limits liability for fraud, dishonest misrepresentation or wilful concealment, whether by the Seller or its agents. The carve-out covers the cap, basket, time limits, non-reliance, disclosure and knowledge provisions.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out expressly. Do not rely on general principles of public policy.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the limitation and non-reliance language would purport to cover fraud, which should never be capped.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only against specific, fairly disclosed items in reasonable detail. No general disclosure of data-room or public-register contents.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 1.1, 1.2 and the Schedule 7 reliance on the data room and public records.
- **Reason:** General data-room disclosure would waive every warranty against everything in roughly a dozen documents, which hollows out the warranty package.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for matters the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** An express pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge or diligence. Known issues are handled through specific indemnities or price, not warranty claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 8.3, delete the "discoverable" language, and insert an express pro-sandbagging clause.
- **Reason:** The Buyer already knows of the DD-002 to DD-012 issues, so an anti-sandbagging clause would bar claims for exactly those matters. Australian law on sandbagging is not settled, so the wording must be express.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent, which is deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3, 6.3). The disclosure confirms no final consent and no evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** Written Bluefen consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions as a condition precedent to Completion. If the Buyer waives it, a price adjustment or escrow sized to the revenue at risk, plus a specific indemnity for loss of the contract.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent, not an endeavours obligation.
- **Reason:** Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m (roughly 30%) of FY26 revenue, and endeavours wording leaves the Buyer funding that loss.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release to be provided after Completion (cl 2, 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Under the debt-free, cash-free basis, repayment at Completion from the price under a payout letter. All security, including PPSR registrations and any share charge, discharged at Completion. Price adjusted for the debt.
- **Recommendation:** Pay out and release at Completion.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with AUD 3.2m of debt and possibly an encumbrance over the shares, with no certainty of release.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses, described as "a matter for the Seller," omitted from the funds flow, with no treatment of payroll tax or superannuation.
- **Buyer wants:** Treated as a Seller cost, deducted from the price as a debt-like item, or paid by the Seller through payroll at Completion. The deduction includes employer on-costs.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct the full cost, including on-costs, from the price. On-costs are indicatively around AUD 70k, so the all-in cost may be about AUD 490k. This must be confirmed by payroll advisers, including the NSW payroll tax rate and whether the bonuses count as ordinary time earnings for superannuation.
- **Reason:** If the funds flow omits the bonuses, the company bears the cost after Completion.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** The Seller pays the AUD 180k outstanding before Completion, or it is deducted from the price. A confirmatory assignment of Project Materials is delivered at Completion. A specific indemnity covers all Ironquay claims, including IP ownership, third-party infringement, costs and loss of use, outside the de minimis, basket and general cap. The Buyer obtains bank evidence of non-payment, since the AUD 180k figure is not independently verified.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." Require payment, assignment and a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** Under clause 7.3, transfer of the materials depends on payment and the company may not own the SOW3 IP until then, so paying the balance alone does not cure the title gap.

## SPA-N-012: Export and privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary" and "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6, Schedule 6). The disclosure says the file may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, and that access, scope and notification status are unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** A forensic investigation before signing. A determination of whether this is an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC, which would require OAIC and individual notification. Seller bears the cost of investigation, notification and remediation. A specific indemnity, uncapped or separately capped. A warranty that no other notifiable breach has occurred. Retention or escrow pending the outcome.
- **Recommendation:** Pre-signing forensic report, specific indemnity and retention.
- **Reason:** The Seller's own disclosure cannot establish whether there was access or whether notification is required, so "not material" is unsupported. The NDB scheme generally expects an assessment within 30 days, and the matter was still preliminary on 22 September. The Buyer needs to check compliance now.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k, described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of the contracts, terms, termination rights and any commitments beyond Completion. The Buyer should check whether the three AUD 110k renewals were split to sit under approval thresholds. Interim covenant requiring Buyer consent to new or renewed commitments. Non-ordinary-course commitments treated as debt-like.
- **Recommendation:** Verify before accepting the ordinary-course characterisation. Add an interim covenant.
- **Reason:** The disclosure does not confirm whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, so the characterisation cannot yet be relied on.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime for all claims (cl 9.3, 12.3, 12.8, 13, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories:
  - General warranties: capped, subject to thresholds, 24 months.
  - Fundamental (title, capacity, authority): full price, 6 years, no thresholds.
  - Tax: standalone indemnity, no thresholds, extended period.
  - Specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy, Sandbar, Mossvale): no thresholds, outside the general cap.
  - Fraud: uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime.
- **Reason:** Applying general-warranty thresholds to title, tax and known liabilities that are specific by nature would make the Buyer's protection largely illusory.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass as holder of 100%.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current ASIC company extract, inspection of the original register, share certificates and transfer history, and a PPSR search against the shares and the company (including any Riverlark security). A title and no-encumbrance warranty, treated as fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent searches before signing and make title a fundamental warranty.
- **Reason:** The register is the Seller's own document and is not verification, and an undisclosed encumbrance (such as a Riverlark share charge) could defeat clean title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties treated as "settled" under the general regime, meaning the 4.8m cap and 18-month limit.
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity covering all taxes, including payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses, outside the cap, basket and de minimis, with a limitation period of 6 years or the ATO amendment period. Full IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement and contractor-created IP, with ownership treated as fundamental.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation and treat both as open.
- **Reason:** Tax exposure and IP ownership are not risks that a general cap should absorb, and the Ironquay matter already shows IP ownership can be defective.

---

## Priority Actions
1. **Reject the reviewer note.** Treat all 16 items as open.
2. **Update the disclosure to today's date.** Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the privacy status may have changed since 22 September.
3. **Request the following:**
   - Bluefen consent and clause 11.3 evidence
   - Riverlark payout letter and PPSR search
   - Bonus agreements and payroll calculations
   - Ironquay bank records and assignment
   - Privacy forensic report and NDB assessment status
   - Sandbar contracts
   - Office lease and Mossvale provisions
   - ASIC extract and share register
4. **Get NSW counsel to confirm** limitation periods, sandbagging position and the payroll tax and superannuation figures before the mark-up goes out.
